newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Placer confident on Venezuelan gold mine.
newsitem.headline: Placer confident on Venezuelan gold mine.

text.p: Canadian mining company Placer Dome Inc, appearing to rule out any long delay on its Las Cristinas gold mine project in Venezuela, said it welcomed the intention of its joint venture partner to resolve issues separating them.

Placer Dome President for Latin America William Hayes said the company "welcomed the intention shown by (Venezuelan state-owned holding) Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) to solve this week issues that hold up the signing of three contracts."
These contracts, including one on shareholding and another on electricity supply, "are essential to guarantee the financing of our joint project," he said in a Saturday press release.
Placer Dome said that apart from these three issues, "no other fundamental problem prevents the financing" from going ahead.

Placer holds a 70 percent stake in the Las Cristinas project, in south-eastern Bolivar state. CGV holds the other 30 percent. The project will require investment of $636 million in the next two years, the Placer statement said.
Construction was initially set to begin a month ago. The mine is projected to produce 450,000 ounces of gold a year for at least 16 years and forms a big part of Placer's growth strategy.
